text:
carlos: heads up — on the new mosaic-7b import I'm seeing weird output where the assistant replies start with a weird token sequence instead of expected BOS. looked into tokenizer ids and found an off-by-one for several special tokens after running our hf->redwood conversion.

maya: can you paste the quick diff you ran?

carlos: sure. HF tokenizer returns: `{'bos_token_id': 1, 'eos_token_id': 2, 'pad_token_id': 0}`. after import our runtime reports: `{'bos_token_id': 2, 'eos_token_id': 3, 'pad_token_id': 1}`. same vocab file, but added_tokens.json has 4 entries.

carlos: minimal repro I used:
```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('my/mosaic-7b-converted')
print(t.convert_tokens_to_ids(['<bos>', '<eos>', '<pad>', '<unk>']))
# on HF: [1, 2, 0, 3]
# after redwood import: [2, 3, 1, 4]
```

tom_r: hmm, that looks like a shift rather than arbitrary remap. any duplicate entries in `added_tokens.json` or tokens that are zero-width / zero-length? tokenizers sometimes dedupe silently.

li: i hit something similar last quarter — root cause was an `added_tokens.json` that included both `"<pad>"` and a zero-width variant `"\u200b"` mapped as special. when merging vocab we end up inserting the new tokens before existing specials, pushing IDs.

maya: also check `config.json` field `tokenizer_class` vs saved tokenizer type. fast_tokenizer vs python tokenizers can differ in how they assign special ids on save/load.

carlos: good call. i grep'ed added_tokens.json and found these entries at top: `"<new_ctrl>"`, `"\u200b"`, `"<pad>"`, `"<bos>"`. the zero-width one was unexpected. we probably imported a file from a preprocessing step that inserted it.

carlos: quick patch i did locally: remove zero-width token from added_tokens and re-run `tokenizer.save_pretrained(...)` then re-import. fixed ids back to expected.

maya: nice. can you share exact commands so ops can bake into conversion pipeline? would like a guard to reject any control/zero-width chars in added tokens.

carlos: steps i ran:
```bash
# prune added tokens with control chars
python tools/prune_added_tokens.py --input added_tokens.json --output added_tokens.clean.json --reject-control-chars
python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('.'); t.save_pretrained('./cleaned')"
# then run hf->redwood-import on ./cleaned
```

maya: can we add a unit test in the importer to assert that special token ids match the HF tokenizer mapping? even a lightweight smoke check would catch this.

tom_r: yes — importer currently trusts the saved `vocab.json` + `added_tokens.json` order. add a post-load sanity check: compare `tokenizer.special_tokens_map` and `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(specials)` against expected ids stored in HF metadata. if mismatch, fail import or emit a warning with `--auto-fix` opt.

li: also note quantized artifacts sometimes re-order token blocks in our packaging step (we concatenate tensors and rewrite indices). we should ensure packaging preserves the token index map. i'll add that to the checklist for quantization runbooks.

ops-bot: regen-artifact job 3492 started by carlos — running conversion with cleaned tokenizer (job link: https://ci.redwood/3492).

carlos: thanks — after regen CI shows model passes convo smoke tests. will follow up with a small PR to importer to block control chars in added tokens + a failing test reproducing the shift.

maya: perfect. assign to you and @tom_r for review? :+1:

tom_r: i'll review. also add a tiny migration script to rewrite old imported models (if we detect the bad pattern) to avoid surprise regressions for existing Dedicated customers.

li: leaving a note: for future bring-ups, always run `python tools/token_check.py --compare-hf --compare-import` as part of the onboarding checklist.

carlos: agreed. i'll add docs in the onboarding checklist and link the PR here once merged.

maya: thanks all — nice quick sleuthing :tada:
